canonical_intent_definition: A subjective, future-oriented, directional, state-changing tendency formed under governed multi-source influence.
canonical_question: I tend to move the next state in which direction?

boundaries.non_equivalence: Need indicates a deficit or requirement; it does not itself express a governed future-state tendency.
Drive supplies pressure; Intent is a qualified subjective tendency.
Desire is not a governed Intent candidate and no Emotion runtime is introduced.

boundaries.relation: may receive an admitted direction later
boundaries.non_equivalence: Goal represents a state direction to maintain, improve, or reach and has separate governance.

boundaries.relation: may be a downstream execution decomposition or an external reference
boundaries.non_equivalence: Task Manager owns task lifecycle, not subjective tendency.

boundaries.relation: may amplify or suppress available evidence
boundaries.non_equivalence: Attention allocates cognitive resources; it is not Intent.
Emotion can influence strength or direction candidates but cannot create or mutate Intent.
Activation is salience/connectivity, not subjective future direction.
Link strength does not prove Intent.
Frequency is not formation or truth.
Environmental pressure is not owned subjective direction.
Social obligation does not automatically become Intent.
Intent competition and dominance do not select a course.
Intent never authorizes or performs Action.
